lines.text: Every July, our school holds its sports day at the stadium near the river.
This year, more than nine hundred student took part in the events.
The day began with a march past, and each class carry a banner it
lines.note: Tense: 'began' is in the past, so it is 'carried'.

lines.text: had painted the week before. My class chose a eagle as our symbol
lines.note: Article: 'eagle' starts with a vowel sound, so it is 'an eagle'.

lines.text: because we wanted to look fierce. The first race of the morning was the
hundred-metre sprint. Our fastest runner, Daniel, were nervous because he had lost last
lines.note: Agreement: 'our fastest runner' is one person, so it is 'was'.

lines.text: year. When the whistle blew, he ran so quick that nobody could catch him.
lines.note: Word form: 'ran' is a verb, so it takes the adverb 'quickly'.

lines.text: The whole class jumped up and cheer until our throats were sore.
lines.note: Tense: 'jumped up and cheered' — both verbs are in the past.

lines.text: In the afternoon, the teachers ran a relay against the parents and lost badly.
The best moment came at the end, when both of our relay team won.
My classmates still talks about that day whenever we pass the stadium.
lines.note: Agreement: 'my classmates' is plural, so it is 'talk'.

lines.text: Next year we hope to win the tug-of-war as well.
